nodes.title: rc3 adopter feedback: upgrade and adoption friction

acceptance: A helper in version_skew.py lists every specy-road and specyrd executable on PATH in PATH order with its resolved target (symlinks followed) and whether it belongs to the running interpreter (sys.prefix); specy-road doctor prints that list and warns when the first one on PATH is not the running install; a test builds a PATH with two fake launchers and asserts the order and the warning

validate warns (non-fatal) when the 'Written by specy-road X' line of any managed block (root AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) names a version other than the running one, even when .specyrd/manifest.json specyrd_version matches; the warning names the file, both versions and specy-road upgrade; a test pins manifest at the running version with a block from an older one
Out of scope: changing the existing older-than-recorded and pin warnings, installing or removing launchers, and the upgrade output (M13.2)
nodes.title: Say which install is running and flag managed blocks an older version wrote

acceptance: upgrade's first lines name the running version, sys.prefix and the launcher list from M13.1; under --dry-run the first line reads 'previewing what specy-road <version> would write'

upgrade --dry-run also runs validate, against a temporary copy of the project with the refreshes applied (the checkout is never written), prints its errors and exits with validate's code; a test injects a validate error the new version raises and asserts --dry-run exits 1 before anything is written

After writing, upgrade checks every file it wrote or rewrote against the project's file-limits caps and names each one its own write pushed over the cap (path, old and new line count, cap); a file already over the cap before the upgrade is not blamed on it; a test covers both

upgrade's help and module docstring name pip, pipx and uv tool upgrades instead of only 'pip install -U'. Out of scope: changing which refreshes run or their order, and digest drift wording beyond pointing at validate's notices
nodes.title: upgrade previews as the new version, validates in a dry run and names files it pushed over the line cap

acceptance: A project setting (agents_block: minimal in .specyrd/manifest.json, default full) makes refresh-stubs and upgrade write a root AGENTS.md block of at most 3 lines that points at .specyrd/AGENTS.md; the default full block gains one line saying why the floor bullets are repeated there; validate's context lines reflect the smaller block; a test renders both

When upgrade or refresh-stubs first creates .specyrd/AGENTS.md it prints the new file's headings and names each heading of the project's own AGENTS.md text (outside the managed block) that matches one of them case-insensitively, with one line saying to compare and drop the stale copy; a test with a duplicated heading asserts the line
Each harness's validate context line ends with a per-harness total in lines and bytes, counting a file imported twice (CLAUDE.md imports) once and saying so
Out of scope: removing the floor bullets from the default block, editing project text outside managed blocks, and rewriting .specyrd/AGENTS.md content
nodes.title: A pointer-only AGENTS.md block option, and upgrade names the project text the new rules file duplicates

acceptance: validate prints one notice per milestone whose rollup is held by policy.milestone_full_review, with the hold reason milestone_review_hold gives and the three ways out (review it with the commands that do so, record it Complete, or set milestone_full_review: false); upgrade shows them because it runs validate; a test pins the notice for a milestone whose leaves are all Complete
why-blocked <ID> on a held milestone prints the same reason and ways out; list-nodes marks a held milestone (for example 'In Progress (review hold)') and its --json output carries the reason

docs/orchestration-review.md's milestone full review section shows the notice and the three ways out. Out of scope: changing when the hold applies (including exempting milestones completed before an upgrade), and the hold's default
nodes.title: A milestone held for its full review says so in validate, list-nodes and why-blocked

acceptance: refresh-profiles (and upgrade, which calls it) writes by default only the bundled profiles a roster entry in roadmap/orchestration.yaml names, plus model-profiles/README.md; --profiles all keeps today's behaviour; a repo with no roster gets only the README and a line naming --profiles all; a test covers roster, no roster and all

The 'matches no model profile' warning names the closest bundled api_id when one differs only in punctuation or a vendor/effort prefix or suffix (claude-opus-5.5 vs claude-opus-5-5; cursor-gpt-5.6-sol-high vs gpt-5.6-sol) and prints the roster line that fixes it; no near match keeps today's text; a test pins both examples
Out of scope: editing the roster automatically, deleting profiles already written, and changing profile content
nodes.title: refresh-profiles installs only the profiles the roster names, and suggests the alias for a near miss

acceptance: docs/install-and-usage.md replaces the --index-url TestPyPI plus --extra-index-url PyPI recipe with: pip download --no-deps of the exact pinned version from TestPyPI, a sha256 check against the published value, then pip install --no-deps of that wheel with dependencies installed from PyPI only; it says why (any dependency could resolve from TestPyPI) and gives the uv equivalent
docs/release-runbook.md's RC announcement step publishes that recipe and the wheel's sha256

Install and upgrade sections cover pip, pipx and uv tool for both final releases and RCs, and a 'Which install is running' subsection shows which -a specy-road specyrd, specy-road --version, resolving a symlinked launcher, and clearing a stale specyrd launcher that makes a second install fail

A docs test asserts no doc pairs a TestPyPI --index-url with --extra-index-url in an install command. Out of scope: publishing to a different index, signing wheels, and code changes to upgrade (M13.2)
nodes.title: Safe release-candidate install recipe, pipx and uv tool upgrades, and checking which binary is on PATH

acceptance: When a stub directory refresh-stubs reports (for example .agents/skills) is a symlink, the report prints the resolved path once, or notes 'symlink to <target>', instead of listing the same files twice under two names; a test with a symlinked skills dir pins it

When an upgrade or refresh adds a .gitignore rule, it lists files already in the tree that the new rule matches, marking tracked ones (git keeps tracking them) and untracked ones (now hidden), at most 20 then a count; a test with one tracked and one untracked match pins the lines

session end, when the shell's derived id has no record and it ends the user's only live session, leads with the session it ended and why (for example 'ended your live session <A> (this shell's id <B> has no record)'); behaviour unchanged; a test pins the text
Out of scope: changing which ignore rules ship, untracking files, and session end behaviour
nodes.title: Clearer notices: symlinked skill dirs, new ignore rules over tracked files, and session end
